submission.justification:
Sensor-T3 has the best unirradiated resolution (6.0 um) but its hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2 is 82.0% due to strong charge trapping, failing the hard >=97% end-of-life requirement, so it is excluded. Sensor-T2 keeps efficiency (99.2%) but has the worst resolution (14 um). Sensor-T1 is the best remaining option: 98.5% hit efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2 (meets the hard constraint) and a 9.0 um single-hit resolution, better than T2. I recommend 150 um, the only thickness for which resolution was simulated (2025 summary) and the thickness I could reasonably assume for the irradiation campaign. Caveats: the documents do not provide thickness-dependent resolution or irradiated efficiency for other thicknesses, so I could not verify whether a thinner or thicker T1 would do better; thinner sensors would lose signal and risk the efficiency margin (only 1.5% above the requirement), so I did not move away from the validated thickness. The 9 um resolution is unirradiated; post-irradiation resolution was not measured. Readout (50x50 um pixels), cooling (CO2 at -35 C) and power (7 W/module) are compatible with T1.</justification>
